message:
Here is what I could verify, and what I could not.
**The two saved homes — recorded details only**
Both lookups confirmed identity by listing URL, but both are cached snapshots.
Neither was refreshed, so the price and availability are not verified as current.
Confirm with the agent.
| | Bonfield Road, London, SE13 | Unex Tower, 7 Station Street, London, E15 |
|---|---|---|
| Recorded rent | £1,875 pcm | £2,300 pcm |
| Recorded type | 1 bed Flat | 1 bed Flat |
| Recorded amenities | No Agent Fees, Property Reference 3075081 | Concierge, Garden, Furnished |
| Available from | Contact agent | Contact agent |
| Listing | onthemarket.com/details/20567130 | onthemarket.com/details/14951549 |
**Against your two separate ceilings (£2,000 rent / £2,150 rent plus commute, two office days)**
- **Bonfield Road:** recorded rent £1,875 is under the £2,000 rent cap, leaving £275 of the £2,150 combined ceiling for travel.
Whether it fits depends on a travel cost I could not verify for this listing.
- **Unex Tower:** recorded rent £2,300 exceeds the £2,000 rent cap by £300, and the rent alone already exceeds the £2,150 combined ceiling.
It fails on the recorded price regardless of travel cost.
**Self-contained whole flat — not verified for either.** Both are recorded as "1 bed Flat" and neither is flagged as a studio, shared room or en-suite room.
But the records contain no explicit statement that each is a self-contained whole flat with its own kitchen and entrance, and no floor plan or tenancy details.
Treat "whole flat" as unconfirmed for both.
**Stratford to Bank — the 26-single-trip what-if**
I could not price this.
The TfL Journey Planner returned "could not verify this journey for the requested time" on two attempts, so I have no actual current single fare for Stratford to Bank, and I will not substitute a daily cap or a zone-based guess for it.
The 26 × single fare figure therefore cannot be calculated from verified data.
You can check the current single fare at tfl.gov.uk or on the TfL Go app.
**Zonal caps and Travelcard (TfL, adult, effective 1 March 2026, zones 1-3)**
These are zone-based prices, not a verified route price for either address
- Daily PAYG cap: £10.50
- Weekly Travelcard: £52.50
- Monthly Travelcard: £201.60
- PAYG at two office days a week: about £21.00 per week, about £91.00 per month (daily cap × 2 days, averaged over 52/12 weeks)
Important caveats: the PAYG figures are cap-based upper bounds, not verified single or return fares, and actual singles may cost less.
The zone selection does not verify that Lewisham or Stratford, or the whole route to Bank, sits in zones 1-3.
Student discount applies to Travelcards, not PAYG singles.
**Weather, Saturday 24 October, 11:00 (Open-Meteo forecast)**
I could not resolve Lewisham or Stratford as separate locations, so this is a single London-wide forecast, not area-specific: 8.4°C, overcast, feels like 4.4°C, humidity 66%, wind 15.5, UV 1.65, 12% chance of rain.
Cold and breezy for viewings — take a coat.
**Public-transport disruption: not checked.** The TfL line-status service could not be reached, so I have no disruption information for either route.
Check tfl.gov.uk/status before you travel on the day.
**Is either worth pursuing?**
- **Bonfield Road** is the only one of the two that clears your rent cap on the recorded price, so it is the one worth a viewing enquiry — but ask the agent to confirm the rent is current, that it is a self-contained whole flat, and the exact availability, and check the actual commute and fare yourself.
- **Unex Tower** fails your rent cap and your combined ceiling on the recorded price.
It would only become relevant if the asking rent has dropped substantially, which I cannot verify.
**What I could not verify, in summary:** current rent and availability for either flat
 that either is a self-contained whole flat
 the Stratford to Bank single fare and the 26-trip total
 per-listing monthly travel cost
 that either address is in zones 1-3
 area-specific weather
Note: some commute claims could not be verified and have been removed from this answer.
